author_note: independent reference authored without access to the tool code
reference: Hand-built rule-table corpus for the PPE Decision Matrix: hierarchy-of-controls gating (all four levels assessed, eliminated hazard, each single level not assessed, state after controls unknown), required-context insufficient-data cases, oxygen-deficiency rejection of filtering respirators, EN 14387 gas filter type per substance from HSG53, particle filter class from PF_req = C/OEL against HSG53 assigned protection factors (analytic boundaries plus 6 seeded random cases), Directive 2003/10/EC action-value boundaries (plus 6 seeded random cases), EN 166 fields of use, arc rating >= incident energy, fall-arrest anchorage, compatibility (facial hair, eyewear + respirator seal) and two multi-hazard matrix cases. Every case also asserts that no product is named and no risk is declared acceptable. Categorical expectations are derived from the quoted source text, not from the tool's rule table.
reference_citations: HSE HSG53 'Respiratory protective equipment at work', 4th ed. 2013 https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/priced/hsg53.pdf - oxygen-deficiency warning, paras 19, 22, 45, 71-72, 80, APF table, EN 14387 filter type table, table 3
ISO 45001:2018 cl. 8.1.2 a)-e), wording as reproduced at https://preteshbiswas.com/2023/09/30/iso-450012018-clause-8-1-2-eliminating-hazards-and-reducing-ohs-risks/ (standard itself not read)
EN 166:2001 field-of-use symbols 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, as reproduced at https://skanwear.com/blogs/ppe-standards/en-166 (standard itself not read)
specs/10.md (validation and acceptance criteria), specs/00-common.md 0.5; bench/ppedecision/ref.py
tolerance: Categorical and boolean checks are exact: the tool is a discrete rule engine and any difference is a logic difference. The two numeric checks (required protection factor C/OEL and minimum arc rating) are single divisions or copies of an input, so relative 1e-9 covers floating-point rounding only. Action-value comparisons use the directive's own inequalities with no margin.

not_benchmarked: EN 14387 type B vs E for HCl and other acid inorganic gases: HSG53 wording overlaps, so no such case
particle class where HSG53 APF and EN 149 nominal protection factors disagree (PF_req in (10,12] and (20,50]): ref.py excludes that band; only the class-1/2 exclusion is asserted at PF 30
EN 352 attenuation / EN ISO 4869-2 SNR-HML selection (covered by noiseexposure bench; not read here)
welding shade numbers (EN 169), glove performance levels, footwear S-classes, EN ISO 20471 class: standards not read
COMP-R-003..007 heuristics (helmet + muffs, muffs + eyewear, corrective lenses, chemical clothing on heat task, gloves near rotating parts): no source read fixes them
RESP-R-003 (confined space with oxygen declared normal -> measure) and HOC-R-004 (high severity without upper controls): tool heuristics without an independent basis
arc incident energy exactly 0 and fall clearance / rescue arithmetic: semantics not fixed by a source read
JSA handoff import, CSV/PDF layout, seven-language labels, images: UI/exchange, not the safety decision
edition currency of EN standards (spec asks to confirm; not done here)
coverage: Covers the spec 10 headline claims: PPE only against residual hazard after the hierarchy step; insufficient data when required context is unknown; oxygen-deficiency rejection of filtering respirators (the named negative test); generic class/standard family per column for eye/face, hearing, respiratory, head, hand, foot, body and fall with no product names; compatibility warnings (eyewear + respirator seal, facial hair); hazard -> rule -> source trace and rule IDs surviving export; and PPE never declaring the risk acceptable.
